      <title>Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya</link>
      <description><p>No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia</p><p>A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p>The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe</link>
      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa</link>
      <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba</link>
      <description><p>New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people</p><p>• <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/16/slave-trade-wealth-britain-financial-system-bank-of-england-enslaved-africans">Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds</a></p><p>British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.</p><p>Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/race-to-be-next-un-secretary-general-exposes-divisions-among-world-powers</link>
      <description><p>Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner</p><p>The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers.       <title>Australian politics live: Tehan says Bowen should resign over Cop; Taylor pays tribute to ‘kind, gentle’ Meldrum</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/nov/23/anthony-albanese-digital-duty-of-care-labor-greens-coalition-one-nation-angus-taylor-pauline-hanson-penny-wong-ai-ntwnfb</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p><strong>‘Very difficult to bridge that divide’: Murray Watt</strong></p><p>Cabinet minister <strong>Murray Watt</strong> says it’s increasingly difficult to bridge the divide between nations on climate policy after a frustrating Cop summit that didn’t reach a final agreement.</p><p>It’s obviously a very deeply disappointing outcome that the cover decision was not agreed to by all nations.</p><p>I think what this shows is a very challenging international environment at the moment to reach agreement on almost anything and particularly a situation like this where you’ve got fossil fuel producers on the one hand and other countries that are experiencing very serious impacts from climate change.</p><p>We’re seeing much greater defence engagement between Australia and Japan, Australia and the Philippines, and the Philippines and Japan.</p><p>Even though I think it doesn’t quite come across in its overall score, that US defence relationship in the region is stronger, which is helping Australia.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/nov/23/anthony-albanese-digital-duty-of-care-labor-greens-coalition-one-nation-angus-taylor-pauline-hanson-penny-wong-ai-ntwnfb">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm event</p><p>With their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness.       <title>Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/europe-elections-supercycle-could-shake-eu-foundations</link>
      <description><p>As nationalist, Eurosceptic parties surge in four of the bloc’s biggest member states, the coming year’s polls could test its resilience like never before</p><p>In late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany. The EU had 15 member states and pro-European, centre-left parties were in power – either alone or in coalitions – in all but two of them.</p><p>Brisk economic growth was lifting living standards. Eastward enlargement was under way. In Washington, Bill Clinton was pursuing the same brand of “third way” centrism as a middle path between free-market capitalism and traditional socialism. The EU felt like it had the tide of history behind it.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/europe-elections-supercycle-could-shake-eu-foundations">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>After chaos at airlines, banks and companies from Microsoft to Apple, people have become convinced the world’s systems are under attack</p><p>Nicole Reindorf’s American Airlines flight was ready for takeoff in Phoenix when the pilot came on the intercom and announced what was to become the longest nationwide aviation shutdown since <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/september11">9/11</a>.</p><p>Reindorf, 70, had seen the headlines hours before about a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/live/2026/nov/13/microsoft-outage-down-today-live-update-outlook-teams-365-when-fixed-latest-status-cause-news">global Microsoft outage</a>. She immediately suspected the two were linked in some way by AI-related threats – and that she would not get to the wedding of her best friend’s son in California.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/22/hacks-ai-internet-outages-airlines-banks-microsoft-apple">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Two weeks after Democrats flipped Congress, conservative outlets are having conversations on whether to distance themselves from Trump or double down on Maga</p><p>As a so-called “blue wave” crashed across the country on the night of 3 November, conservative hosts and commentators on Fox News <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/04/trump-blames-fox-news-republican-losses">displayed an almost virtuosic ability to avoid directly blaming Donald Trump</a> for the Republican party’s defeat, instead pinning the blame on impertinent voters who didn’t grasp the strength of the economy.</p><p>“In some sense, Mr Trump was too successful in the first year and didn’t sell it enough in the second year,” said Larry Kudlow, a Fox Business Network host who served as the president’s director of the National Economic Council during his first administration.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/conservative-media-trump-midterm-elections-results">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/19/who-are-anthropic-founders">Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?</a></p></li></ul><p>As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&amp;P 500 closed in correction territory.</p><p>Anthropic’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/19/anthropic-public-trading-ipo">record-breaking IPO</a> failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some <a href="https://www.wsj.com/finance/stocks/anthropics-ipo-bust-punctuates-4-trillion-ai-wipeout-on-wall-street-f1f1ec90?mod=WSJ_home_mediumtopper_pos_1">$4tn in market value</a> this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/20/global-stock-markets-slump-anthropic-ipo-ai-sell-off">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The two sides have come to agreements on food and drink, emissions trading and the youth exchange scheme</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/20/fallout-over-tuition-fees-may-snag-burnhams-eu-deal-say-insiders">Burnham has agreed EU reset deal with tuition fees issue unresolved, says No 10</a></p></li></ul><p>After months of on-off negotiations, leaks and late nights, the EU and UK have agreed <a href="https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/statement_26_2512">a 12-page statement</a> setting out the next steps in their relationship. What exactly have they agreed?</p><p>• This article was amended on 22 November 2026. An earlier version incorrectly said that wine was included in the food and drink deal.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/20/what-is-in-deal-between-uk-eu-explainer">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <media:content width="460" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/7dc3c60fa8338bc5ee1369a6d31d699690231550/148_0_2427_1942/master/2427.jpg?width=460&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=53595cf4eae7e929b79e46d39943b98e">

      <description><p>UK central bank will want to avoid echoes of expensive US Federal Reserve revamp that led to Trump clash</p><p>Andrew Bailey may spend his days closely watching developments in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/strait-of-hormuz">strait of Hormuz</a> or US stock markets for signs of shocks to the global economy – but the Bank of England’s governor has a £160m problem brewing much closer to home.</p><p>A secretive major revamp of the Bank’s historic headquarters in the heart of London’s Square Mile presents a huge test of Bailey’s project management skills.       <description><p>When partners consider finances, when is it ‘my’ money, and when it is ‘our’ money? Guardian readers shared their experiences </p><ul><li><a href="http://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2014/aug/08/end-loveless-marriage-financially-dependent">Private lives: ‘I want to end my marriage but I’m financially dependent</a>’<br></li></ul><p>A survey of about 1,000 Americans found that one in 10 would describe their partner as a financial bully. Our readers, however, insist that that might be a label easily assigned to a partner who is simply being financially responsible.</p><p>When we put out a call to out readers last week to see if any of them had similar experiences, we found that many of you wouldn’t define the actions described as financial bullying. Instead, <a href="https://www.facebook.com/theguardian/posts/10152614052646323">quite a number of you insisted</a> that keeping track of your partner’s expenses was simply budgeting and being financially responsible.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/us-money-blog/2014/aug/14/relationships-finances-bullying-abuse-dependent-equality">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘I ain’t goin nowhere’: Gullah Geechee people fight off developers with a historic referendum</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/jan/22/gullah-geechee-georgia-development-referendum</link>
      <description><p>A citizen referendum, only the second of its kind in Georgia history, seeks to block a zoning amendment</p><p>Ire Gene Grovner stood behind his house on a recent morning, between chicken pens on one side and rows of winter collard greens on the other, holding a knife and skinning a raccoon splayed across a wood post.</p><p>“The meat is good roasted,” Grovner said. He pointed to the collards, a burst of green in the winter cold, and the chickens, with their eggs. “If you ain’t lazy, you can live good here,” he said, referring to Sapelo Island off the coast of southern <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/georgia-news">Georgia</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/jan/22/gullah-geechee-georgia-development-referendum">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Liverpool hand Pochettino nightmare Manchester United start after Yoro sees red</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Green shoots of recovery have lasted longer in a blast furnace than in the Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United. On another abysmal Anfield day for the fallen giants of Manchester, Pochettino endured a baptism of fire from the eighth minute onwards when Leny Yoro was sent off for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity. Liverpool would not be denied anything else while tormenting their old rivals yet again.</p><p>Andoni Iraola indulged in his first fist-pumps towards the Kop after an utterly dominant, comfortable win illuminated by Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz brilliance plus goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz. Liverpool’s two creative forces were also on the scoresheet as Ngumoha became the youngster scorer in the fixture’s Premier League history.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/hull-brighton-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment.</p><p>Make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/brighton-rocking-premier-league-elite-title-challenge">the headline-grabbing moments</a>, these games are the ones which can trip you up the most.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/hull-brighton-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Manchester City’s WSL title bid hit by Spurs after Vinberg and Naz’s late double</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/manchester-city-tottenham-wsl-match-report</link>
      <description><p>This most unpredictable and evenly contested Women’s Super League campaign took another unexpected twist as Manchester City missed the chance to return to the top of the table as they suffered a second successive defeat, by virtue of a terrific performance from a Tottenham side who moved within three points of the European places.</p><p>The shock result came just 24 hours after City’s title rivals Chelsea had dropped points at Liverpool. It was the first time City had failed to win a home league match during Andrée Jeglertz’s 16 months in charge, let alone lose.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/manchester-city-tottenham-wsl-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and match-winning assist against Ipswich.</p><p>That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/tottenham-ipswich-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/coventry-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-premier-league">that the new manager</a> bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.</p><p>Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/coventry-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out</link>
      <description><p>Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement</p><p>César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like <em>not</em> being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot.</p><p>It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player</p><p>Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.</p><p>He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah.       <title>‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.</p><p>It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/aston-villa-sunderland-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>For <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/aston-villa">Aston Villa</a>, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago.</p><p>Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/aston-villa-sunderland-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Scottish Premiership roundup: Dundee left reeling after 8-0 mauling by Hearts</title>

      <description><ul><li><p>Steven Pressley: ‘I’m embarrassed … I apologise’ </p></li><li><p>Celtic 4-1 St Mirren; Rangers 2-1 Motherwell</p></li></ul><p>Wouter Vrancken said <strong>Hearts</strong>’ remarkable 8-0 demolition of 10-man <strong>Dundee</strong> was his team’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle.</p><p>Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kaboré both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal completing the rout. The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:10:28 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in Constitution</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261122-french-right-backs-macron-s-plan-to-put-public-spending-limits-in-constitution</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, just months before the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4bea9e76-e66c-11f1-b8f3-f96315fbf1b4</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 18:09:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg">AFP - STEPHANIE LECOCQ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-students-and-unions-unite-for-sixth-weekend-of-protests-across-france</link><description>
Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7ad79414-e5c2-11f1-8bc6-7d93519529c2</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:43:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg">AFP - GUILLAUME SALIGOT</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-french-court-finds-racism-played-role-in-police-beating-of-black-music-producer</link><description>
A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eadc87ac-e58a-11f1-b7fe-efd3e07e368d</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:41:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-national-assembly-backs-greater-legal-protection-for-police-using-firearms</link><description>
France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a15be40c-e589-11f1-9ce2-a7af964aafae</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:44:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nicolas Economou</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-former-pm-de-villepin-launches-20207-presidential-bid-with-warning-to-far-right</link><description>
Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf6f11fc-e589-11f1-b2ac-0d673b4c7b00</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:02:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg">AP Photo/Aurelien Morissard - Aurelien Morissard</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France must change or 'risk losing' overseas territories, former PM tells RFI</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-france-must-change-or-risk-losing-overseas-territories-former-pm-tells-rfi-manuel-valls</link><description>
France's territories outside Europe are a major strategic asset, giving it a foothold on five continents and in three oceans. Yet Paris has long been accused of neglecting the nearly 3 million people living outside mainland France, who face deep economic and social inequalities. With calls for independence growing, former prime minister Manuel Valls warns that France risks losing its overseas territories unless it radically changes its relationship with them.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c2eb5f78-e343-11f1-ac1e-392da9561c55</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:31:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg">© AFP - DELPHINE MAYEUR </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French Greens candidate gives hard-left Mélenchon a boost in presidential race</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-greens-candidate-gives-hard-left-melenchon-a-boost-in-presidential-race</link><description>
French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has said an alliance with the Greens "should be possible", after the head of the Greens tentatively agreed to back him, angering moderates on the centre-left. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">40b0fb0e-e4dc-11f1-a123-31d05317ef57</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:04:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg">© REUTERS - Tom Nicholson </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Depardieu and Houellebecq accused of gang rape on French film set</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-depardieu-and-houellebecq-accused-of-gang-rape-on-french-film-set</link><description>
Paris prosecutors have opened an investigation after an actress filed a complaint alleging that she was raped by a group including actor Gérard Depardieu and high-profile French author Michel Houellebecq on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec3acb0c-e4dd-11f1-9619-3935a39ed096</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:24:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg">REUTERS - Gonzalo Fuentes</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France probes suspected leaks from interior ministry to far-right National Rally</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-france-probes-suspected-leaks-from-interior-ministry-to-far-right-national-rally</link><description>
France has opened a probe into suspicions that a senior official at the interior ministry leaked secret information to the far-right National Rally (RN) party, which is itself facing a number of investigations, prosecutors have said.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5be0a25a-e4b2-11f1-be46-714476ef8919</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:55:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg">© Pascal Guyot / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French union leader warns strikes will continue without higher wages</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-union-leader-warns-strikes-will-continue-without-higher-wages-cgt-sophie-binet-interview</link><description>
French trade unions have promised to call more strikes and demonstrations, arguing that a government proposal to increase the minimum wage fails to address the social crisis that has spurred protests across the country. Sophie Binet, head of the CGT union, says even after six weeks of action, workers and students are more determined than ever to keep up the fight.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37c8b342-e40f-11f1-a821-bd0c1d2fd9c6</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 06:07:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© REUTERS - Sarah Meyssonnier </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight on France</category><title>Podcast: Living on the breadline, France's 35-hour week and a divisive tax</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/podcasts/spotlight-on-france/20261119-podcast-living-on-minimum-wage-smic-35-hour-working-week-france-second-biggest-tax-csg</link><description>
The French government's decision to raise the minimum wage has failed to satisfy protesters struggling to make ends meet amid the cost-of-living crisis. Also, did the introduction of the 35-hour working week actually help reduce unemployment? The evidence is mixed. And a look at the history of France's second-largest tax, the CSG, and why it's dividing politicians. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8a275ba4-e41c-11f1-8716-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-153-light-blue.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8a275ba4-e41c-11f1-8716-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-153-light-blue.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">da07160a-e41c-11f1-9424-dd481487d627</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:19:04 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France raises bird flu alert to highest level as infections spread across Europe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261119-france-raises-bird-flu-alert-to-highest-level-as-infections-spread-across-europe</link><description>
France is raising its avian flu alert to the highest level from Friday, bringing new restrictions on poultry movements as authorities seek to contain the spread of the virus. The decision comes amid a rise in infections among wild birds across Europe, particularly along migration routes crossing France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eff2afda-e3f7-11f1-a0c0-bdb47d3d53b3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:12:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png">© GAIZKA IROZ / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France rejects 'absurd' Russian claims of direct involvement in Ukraine war</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-france-rejects-absurd-russian-claims-of-direct-involvement-in-ukraine-war</link><description>
The French government on Tuesday dismissed Russian accusations that France is directly involved in the war in Ukraine, following an RFI investigation which revealed a small number of French soldiers have been carrying out training and equipment maintenance missions on Ukrainian territory. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ffdd448e-e346-11f1-831b-65a66bd770f6</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:39:09 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg">AFP - BERTRAND GUAY</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French interior minister accused of 'exaggerating' police protest injury figures</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-french-interior-minister-accused-of-exaggerating-police-protest-injury-figures</link><description>
A group of lawyers have called for an investigation into French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez who they accuse of "spreading false information" about the number of injuries suffered by law enforcement officers since the start of the current protest movement, which they say was used "to justify a disproportionate use of force" against high school protesters.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">294b16e6-e335-11f1-af18-6757e9484dfb</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:09:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg">AFP - SEBASTIEN BOZON</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'We weren't afraid of the future': France's student protests today and in May '68</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-we-weren-t-afraid-of-the-future-france-s-student-protests-today-and-in-may-68</link><description>
As students across France continue demonstrating against conditions in schools, the movement has drawn inevitable comparisons with the biggest student protests in the country's history – those of May 1968. While this date remains a rallying cry for many young French people, they are calling for change in a world that has altered profoundly in the past 58 years.

Deux grandes revendications sont au centre du mouvement : avenir meilleur pour la jeunesse et contre la vie chère.]]></description><guid isPermaLink="true">https://www.lemonde.fr/international/video/2026/11/22/video-manifestations-de-la-gen-z-et-contre-la-vie-chere-retour-sur-un-week-end-de-mobilisation-en-europe_6814237_3210.html</guid><link>https://www.lemonde.fr/international/video/2026/11/22/video-manifestations-de-la-gen-z-et-contre-la-vie-chere-retour-sur-un-week-end-de-mobilisation-en-europe_6814237_3210.html</link><media:content width="644" height="322" url="https://img.lemde.fr/2026/11/20/688/0/8256/4128/644/322/60/0/9662b3d_ftp-1-pwydkzxt36ye-afp-d86p46w.jpg"><media:description type="plain">Des manifestants défilent avec des banderoles et des drapeaux lors d’une manifestation organisée par « GenZ regelt ! » (La Génération Z s’en charge !) à Francfort-sur-le-Main, dans l’ouest de l’Allemagne, le 20 novembre 2026. Le 20 novembre, des manifestants se sont rassemblés dans toute l’Europe pour dénoncer des problèmes allant du coût élevé de la vie aux dépenses militaires en passant par la crise climatique, intensifiant ainsi la pression sur les dirigeants politiques qu’ils accusent d’ignorer les préoccupations des jeunes. Ces rassemblements, coordonnés par une coalition dirigée par des jeunes et regroupant plus de 50 associations, sont alimentés par des revendications qui varient d’un endroit à l’autre, notamment les conflits à l’étranger, les loyers élevés et la détérioration des conditions d’apprentissage dans les écoles et les universités. <rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title>L'actualité économique et politique en Europe - RFI</title><description>Suivez l'actualité en direct dédiée au continent Européen - Les derniers reportages, news et informations en continu en Europe, Emissions, Podcast, dossiers sur RFI.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/</link><lastBuildDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 22:59:09 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Europe</category><title>Espagne: à une semaine des législatives anticipées, la campagne redouble d'intensité</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261122-espagne-%C3%A0-une-semaine-des-l%C3%A9gislatives-anticip%C3%A9es-la-campagne-redouble-d-intensit%C3%A9</link><description>
À une semaine des élections législatives anticipées en Espagne, les deux favoris dans les sondages, Alberto Feijoo, le conservateur du Partido Popular (PP), en tête, et Pedro Sanchez, chef du gouvernement espagnol, socialiste, ont enchaîné les meetings ce week-end. L'écart entre les deux formations se resserre dans les sondages et la campagne redouble d'intensité. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9532a628-e6c6-11f1-829b-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26323717387421.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9532a628-e6c6-11f1-829b-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26323717387421.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">92c82d20-e6be-11f1-8021-c93be014b8d5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 22:58:39 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9532a628-e6c6-11f1-829b-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26323717387421.jpg">© Manu Fernandez / AP Photo</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Ukraine: six morts lors de frappes russes dans la région de Kiev</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261122-ukraine-six-morts-lors-de-frappes-russes-dans-la-r%C3%A9gion-de-kiev</link><description>
La région de Kiev en Ukraine a été harcelée par les drones ce dimanche 22 novembre. Plusieurs dizaines de drones suicide ont attaqué la capitale du pays. Au moins six personnes sont mortes, des dizaines sont blessées ou portées disparues. La journée a commencé par la destruction d’un immeuble de 5 étages où au moins trois personnes sont mortes. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/36f11050-e6a7-11f1-b4f6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326269093758.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/36f11050-e6a7-11f1-b4f6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326269093758.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c0f648e6-e6a8-11f1-b0d0-859de0742277</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 19:13:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/36f11050-e6a7-11f1-b4f6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326269093758.jpg">AP Photo/Efrem Lukatsky - Efrem Lukatsky</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Egalité femmes-hommes: l'objectif est «d'acter des politiques communes au sein de l'UE»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261122-egalit%C3%A9-femmes-hommes-l-objectif-est-d-acter-des-politiques-communes-au-sein-de-l-ue</link><description>
Accélérer la lutte pour l'égalité entre les femmes et les hommes, tel est le thème de la réunion informelle aujourd'hui en Irlande de plusieurs ministres de l'UE chargés de l'Égalité des genres. Que faut-il en attendre ? Où en est-on à l'échelle de l'Union européenne ? Viviane de Beaufort, professeure chercheuse à l'ESSEC Business School, spécialiste du droit de l'Union européenne, de la gouvernance d'entreprise et de l'égalité femmes-hommes, est l'invitée de la mi-journée de RFI.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fc0b9f94-e676-11f1-84cc-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/Viviane-de-Beaufort.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fc0b9f94-e676-11f1-84cc-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/Viviane-de-Beaufort.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">48c01176-e672-11f1-9fa3-214873d4d659</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 13:27:24 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Arthur Ponchelet</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Trois jours après la rencontre Trump-Xi-Poutine, les Britanniques réaffirment leur soutien à l'Ukraine</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261122-trois-jours-apr%C3%A8s-la-rencontre-trump-xi-poutine-les-britanniques-r%C3%A9affirment-leur-soutien-%C3%A0-l-ukraine</link><description>
Le secrétaire d'État britannique à la Défense, Wes Streeting, était à Kiev samedi 21 novembre. Il y a rencontré Volodymyr Zelensky afin de montrer que l'Europe était toujours unie dans son soutien à l'Ukraine, quelques jours après une « déclaration de paix » lors de la rencontre trilatérale entre Vladimir Poutine, Xi Jinping et Donald Trump en Chine, jugée peu crédible par l'Ukraine.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fe432932-e638-11f1-ae27-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26325404656006.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fe432932-e638-11f1-ae27-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26325404656006.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">20adcaa4-e639-11f1-a4f9-a9bfdd752943</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 06:12:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fe432932-e638-11f1-ae27-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26325404656006.jpg">AP Photo/Evgeniy Maloletka - Evgeniy Maloletka</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Lignes de défense</category><title>Les interrogations soulevées par l'opération militaire française «Volia» en Ukraine</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/lignes-de-d%C3%A9fense/20261121-les-interrogations-soulev%C3%A9es-par-l-op%C3%A9ration-militaire-fran%C3%A7aise-volia-en-ukraine</link><description>
Les révélations de RFI, lundi 16 novembre, sur l'existence de l'opération Volia laissent planer certaines incertitudes… La présence de soldats français en Ukraine, des unités régulières non combattantes, soulève deux questions : celle du secret des opérations et celle de la cobelligérance.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75a812c2-e5d9-11f1-af54-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324615525252.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/75a812c2-e5d9-11f1-af54-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324615525252.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ea01bfa6-e449-11f1-be06-2fcae2cf3e8a</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 23:03:23 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Franck Alexandre</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Opposé à l'accueil de demandeurs d'asile, un second village anglais proclame son indépendance</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261121-oppos%C3%A9-%C3%A0-l-accueil-de-demandeurs-d-asile-un-second-village-anglais-proclame-son-ind%C3%A9pendance</link><description>
Dans le Suffolk, un village anglais a voté symboliquement pour quitter le Royaume-Uni. À Barnham, les habitants protestent contre un projet gouvernemental d'hébergement de demandeurs d'asile sur une ancienne base militaire.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d51c170e-e5fb-11f1-832e-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/Entrance-to-RAF-Barnham-geograph-org-uk-4703233.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d51c170e-e5fb-11f1-832e-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/Entrance-to-RAF-Barnham-geograph-org-uk-4703233.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">31840d9e-e5fc-11f1-b6db-2f15bc42ee66</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 22:37:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d51c170e-e5fb-11f1-832e-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/Entrance-to-RAF-Barnham-geograph-org-uk-4703233.jpg">© JThomas / Entrance to RAF Barnham / CC BY-SA 2.0</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Cargo russe ciblé et survol d'hélicoptère: la Finlande signale une série d'incidents</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261121-cargo-russe-cibl%C3%A9-et-survol-d-h%C3%A9licopt%C3%A8re-la-finlande-signale-une-s%C3%A9rie-d-incidents</link><description>
La Finlande a signalé le survol de son territoire par un hélicoptère russe ce 21 novembre. Quelques heures plus tôt, les autorités finlandaises avaient constaté non loin de leurs côtes une attaque d'un drone contre un navire russe. Récit d'une série d'incidents révélateurs de la tension qui règne dans cette région.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9ec49fc4-e5c8-11f1-9307-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26325577827408.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9ec49fc4-e5c8-11f1-9307-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26325577827408.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bd25570a-e5c9-11f1-a118-1f7de7c155c1</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:58:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9ec49fc4-e5c8-11f1-9307-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26325577827408.jpg">© Finnish Border Guard / Lehtikuva via AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Budget UE: plus de 200 milliards d'euros d'économies proposées, Paris et Berlin font la moue</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261121-budget-ue-plus-de-200-milliards-d-euros-d-%C3%A9conomie-propos%C3%A9es-paris-et-berlin-font-la-moue</link><description>
Le président du Conseil européen, Antonio Costa, a proposé samedi plus de 200 milliards d'euros d'économies et une nouvelle taxe sur le secteur numérique, dans l'espoir de conclure d'ici la fin de l'année les négociations sur le futur budget de l'UE, mais s'est aussitôt attiré les critiques de la France et de l'Allemagne, pour des raisons opposées.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9357043a-e5bc-11f1-b84c-97b2b57f9ccc</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:44:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg">© Yves Herman / REUTERS</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Russie: privés de GTA VI en raison des sanctions, les Russes imaginent une version locale du jeu</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261121-russie-priv%C3%A9s-de-gta-vi-en-raison-des-sanctions-les-russes-imaginent-une-version-locale-du-jeu</link><description>
Malgré les sanctions commerciales imposées à la Russie, des joueurs sont parvenus à se procurer GTA VI grâce à des tutoriels diffusés sur les réseaux sociaux. En attendant la sortie un jour, peut-être, d'une version made in Russia. Vraie possibilité ou fantasme ?
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/93f71f7c-e58c-11f1-9033-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26323604388896.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/93f71f7c-e58c-11f1-9033-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26323604388896.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9e106d10-e58c-11f1-be29-99fc1b265b5d</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:55:11 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/93f71f7c-e58c-11f1-9033-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26323604388896.jpg">AP Photo/Kirsty Wigglesworth - Kirsty Wigglesworth</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Ici l'Europe</category><title>Hubert Védrine : «L’UE en tant que telle n’a jamais participé à une négociation internationale»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/ici-l-europe/20261120-hubert-v%C3%A9drine-l-ue-en-tant-que-telle-n-a-jamais-particip%C3%A9-%C3%A0-une-n%C3%A9gociation-internationale</link><description>
Cette semaine, Caroline de Camaret reçoit Hubert Védrine, ancien secrétaire général de l’Elysée sous la présidence de François Mitterrand et ancien ministre socialiste des Affaires étrangères du gouvernement de Lionel Jospin. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42a8de24-e4f3-11f1-83ae-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Hubert-V%C3%A9drine.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42a8de24-e4f3-11f1-83ae-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/Hubert-V%C3%A9drine.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">26d10eb2-e500-11f1-a146-81b42dba9f2f</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 20:04:59 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Caroline de Camaret (France 24)</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Russie: six personnes placées en détention provisoire dans une affaire de «veuves noires»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-russie-six-personnes-plac%C3%A9es-en-d%C3%A9tention-provisoire-dans-une-affaire-de-veuves-noires</link><description>
C'est une affaire de « veuves noires » qui choque la Russie : dans la région de Volgograd, neuf personnes sont accusées d'avoir organisé un réseau pour récupérer les primes de militaires blessés ou tués en Ukraine, grâce à des mariages fictifs conclus avant l'engagement des soldats dans l'armée. L'enquête vient d'être bouclée : les prévenus risquent jusqu'à 20 ans de prison. Six des neuf accusés ont été placés en détention provisoire dans l'attente du procès.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ec5628ba-dfe4-11f0-9eaa-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25351567398088.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ec5628ba-dfe4-11f0-9eaa-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25351567398088.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0120195e-e511-11f1-9083-078c74fc6df3</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:36:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ec5628ba-dfe4-11f0-9eaa-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25351567398088.jpg">© AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Contre la guerre, pour la jeunesse: vague de manifestations à travers l'Europe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-contre-la-guerre-pour-la-jeunesse-vague-de-manifestations-%C3%A0-travers-l-europe</link><description>
Contre la « militarisation » de la société et la vie chère, pour l'avenir des jeunes, l'éducation, le droit au logement, le climat : des dizaines de milliers de manifestants se mobilisent à travers l'Europe vendredi 20 novembre, sur fond de rejet des institutions. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1853515c-e50e-11f1-8321-3bce4db5bc5f</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:25:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg">© Massimiliano Donati / Getty Images</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Le Danemark accuse la Russie d'avoir tenté d'assassiner un rappeur ukrainien</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-le-danemark-va-expulser-un-diplomate-russe-apr%C3%A8s-la-tentative-d-assassinat-d-un-ukrainien-sur-son-sol</link><description>
Le Danemark va expulser l'attaché de défense de l'ambassade de Russie après la tentative d'assassinat d'un rappeur ukrainien sur son sol, qu'il soupçonne Moscou d'avoir orchestré, a indiqué vendredi 20 novembre le ministre danois des Affaires étrangères. La diplomatie russe a promis de riposter. « Moscou donnera une réponse appropriée », a indiqué la porte-parole du ministère russe des Affaires étrangères, Maria Zakharova, citée par l'agence de presse TASS.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7863937e-e507-11f1-99b0-bbfd8e7adaf9</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:35:50 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg">AFP - EMIL HELMS</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Manifestations en Europe: «Une volonté de converger au niveau transnational et avec d'autres générations»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261120-manifestations-en-europe-une-volont%C3%A9-de-converger-au-niveau-transnational-et-avec-d-autres-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rations</link><description>
La mobilisation contre la vie chère traverse toute l'Europe : des millions de personnes sont attendues dans les rues contre la vie chère et pour le droit au logement. Ce mouvement de fond, lancé à partir de ce vendredi 20 novembre, traduit des réalités communes. Ces luttes peuvent-elles vraiment converger ? Quels modes d'action pour quelles revendications ? L’analyse du sociologue Paolo Stuppia, enseignant à Sciences Po Paris et co-auteur de Géopolitique de la jeunesse – Engagement et (dé)mobilisations, publiée aux éditions Cavalier bleu.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9142dd72-e4f9-11f1-8056-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324446135271.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9142dd72-e4f9-11f1-8056-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324446135271.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a69a8ac8-e4f2-11f1-a69d-dfb7bbed3c72</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:07:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>À la Une: Aleksandar Čupić, le sage à la tête du Parlement serbe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-%C3%A0-la-une-aleksandar-%C4%8Dupi%C4%87-le-sage-%C3%A0-la-t%C3%AAte-du-parlement-serbe</link><description>
Une revue de presse des Balkans en partenariat avec Le Courrier des Balkans.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eb8a088e-e4f2-11f1-8ab1-dffd4ffb6f91</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:41:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg">© Djordje Kojadinovic / Reuters</source><dc:creator>Courrier des Balkans</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>UE/Royaume-Uni: Andy Burnham annonce une «réflexion» en 2027 sur les relations à long terme</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-ue-royaume-uni-andy-burnham-annonce-une-r%C3%A9flexion-en-2027-sur-les-relations-%C3%A0-long-terme</link><description>
Pour son premier sommet avec l’UE, le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham peut s’estimer satisfait. Européens et Britanniques se sont mis d’accord sur trois dossiers concernant les jeunes, les émissions de CO2 et les normes alimentaires. La « remise à zéro » imaginée par son prédécesseur Keir Starmer pour les relations entre Londres et Bruxelles est désormais sur des rails, même si union douanière, libre-circulation et marché unique restent des lignes rouges pour les Britanniques. Les Européens affirment avoir tourné la page du Brexit et se satisfont ouvertement des accords ponctuels comme ceux qui ont été trouvés ce vendredi 20 novembre.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f35856f6-e4f2-11f1-85c2-81e9611d4583</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:30:12 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg">AP Photo/Marius Burgelman - Marius Burgelman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Deux missiles russes tombent en Pologne, Varsovie dénonce «une provocation»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-deux-missiles-russes-tombent-en-pologne-varsovie-d%C3%A9nonce-une-provocation</link><description>
